nodes.name: NF cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of nickel foam (2 cm × 6 cm) was ultrasonically cleaned in acetone for 15 min to remove organic impurities, followed by ultrasonic cleaning in 3 M HCl for 10 min to eliminate surface oxides. It was then rinsed thoroughly with deionized water and ethanol, and dried for later use.
nodes.source_text: A piece of nickel foam (2 cm × 6 cm) was ultrasonically cleaned in acetone for 15 min... and dried for later use.

nodes.name: NiCo2O4 nanoneedles hydrothermal growth
nodes.procedure: 1.09 g Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.3 g Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 2.25 g urea, and 0.278 g NH4F were dissolved in 60 mL deionized water under stirring. The solution was transferred into a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave and heated at 120 °C for 6 h. After cooling to room temperature, the NF was washed with ethanol and deionized water, and freeze-dried to yield NiCo2O4 nanoneedles.

nodes.name: Selenization
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared NF was placed downstream in a quartz tube furnace, with 0.5 g selenium powder upstream. Under an Ar atmosphere, the system was heated to 450 °C at a rate of 5 °C/min and held for 60 min.

nodes.name: Ru impregnation and annealing
nodes.procedure: The resulting NiCo2O4-Se nanoneedles were immersed in a 10 mg/mL RuCl3·3H2O solution for 6 h, then rinsed with ethanol and vacuum-dried at 60 °C overnight. Finally, the sample was annealed at 300 °C for 90 min under Ar (10 °C/min ramp rate) to obtain Ru-NiCo2O4-Se nanoneedles.

nodes.name: Ru-NiCo2O4-Se nanorods complete synthesis
nodes.procedure: Hydrothermal synthesis using modified conditions (0.111 g NH4F, 0.90 g urea, 10 h reaction time) followed by selenization (0.5 g Se powder, 450°C, 60 min Ar), RuCl3 impregnation (10 mg/mL, 6 h), vacuum drying (60°C overnight), and annealing (300°C, 90 min Ar).
nodes.source_text: According to previous studies, the synthesis method is similar to that of Ru-NiCo2O4-Se nanoneedles, except for the use of 0.111 g NH4F, 0.90 g urea, and an extended reaction time of 10 h.

nodes.name: Pt/C and RuO2 electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: 20 mg of noble metal powder (20 wt% Pt/C or RuO2) was dispersed in 1 mL of a mixed solution consisting of ethanol and 5 wt% Nafion. The mixture was ultrasonicated for 60 min to obtain a uniformly dispersed black ink. The resulting ink was then drop-cast onto the surface of NF using a micropipette and dried in an oven at 60 °C to obtain the Pt/C and RuO2 electrodes.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCo₂O₄ nanoneedles possess sharp tips, smooth surfaces, slender needle-like morphology with base diameter ~100 nm; Ru-NiCo₂O₄-Se maintains morphology but surfaces become rougher.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) reveals that the synthesized NiCo₂O₄ nanoneedles possess sharp tips, smooth surfaces, and a slender needle-like morphology... with a base diameter of approximately 100 nm (Fig. 1a, b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-NiCo₂O₄-Se shows lattice spacings of d=0.25 nm (311 plane of NiCo₂O₄) and d=0.23 nm (101 plane of Ru).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image of the Ru-NiCo₂O₄-Se NNS in Fig. 1f shows lattice spacings of d = 0.25 nm and d = 0.23 nm, which correspond to the (311) plane of NiCo₂O₄ and the (101) plane of Ru, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern reveals diffraction rings from (103),(100) planes of Ru and (311),(440) planes of NiCo₂O₄, confirming polycrystalline nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the Ru-NiCo₂O₄-Se NNS (Fig. 1g) clearly reveals diffraction rings attributable to the (103) and (100) planes of Ru, as well as the (311) and (440) planes of NiCo₂O₄, confirming the polycrystalline nature.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni, Co, O, Se, and Ru elements throughout Ru-NiCo₂O₄-Se nanoneedles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping in Fig. 1e indicates a uniform distribution of Ni, Co, O, Se, and Ru elements throughout the nanoneedles.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP analysis reveals Ru content of approximately 1.2 wt% in Ru-NiCo₂O₄-Se.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma (ICP) analysis reveals that the Ru content is approximately 1.2 wt% (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-NiCo₂O₄-Se retains cubic spinel NiCo₂O₄ structure with characteristic peaks at 2θ=18.8°, 36.9°, 44.6°, 59.1°, 65.0°; slight peak shift at 64.9° indicates Ru-support interactions; no distinct Ru peaks due to low content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structures... of NiCo₂O₄, NiCo₂O₄-Se, and Ru-NiCo₂O₄-Se were investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD). As shown in Fig. 1h, NiCo₂O₄ exhibits characteristic diffraction peaks at 2θ = 18.8°, 36.9°, 44.6°, 59.1°, and 65.0°, which correspond to the (111), (220), (311), (400), (511), and (440) planes of the cubic spinel NiCo₂O₄ phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks shift from 856.2/874.0 eV to 855.5/873.3 eV; Co 2p shows Co³⁺ at 780.8/796.4 eV, Co²⁺ at 782.5/798.0 eV with negative shift; Ru 3p shows Ru⁴⁺ at 465.7/488.1 eV and Ru⁰ at 462.3/485.8 eV; Se 3d shifts to higher BE, indicating Ru-NiCo₂O₄-Se electronic interactions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For NiCo₂O₄-Se, two characteristic peaks appear at binding energies (BE) of 856.2 and 874.0 eV... Compared to NiCo₂O₄-Se, the Ni 2p peaks in Ru-NiCo₂O₄-Se shift to lower binding energies... The Ru 3p spectrum displays peaks at 465.7 and 488.1 eV (Ru⁴⁺)... and 462.3 and 485.8 eV (metallic Ru⁰).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows intermediate oxidation state between Ru⁰ and Ru⁴⁺; EXAFS reveals Ru-O at 1.5 Å and Ru-Ru at 2.2 Å bonds, confirming Ru nanoclusters with Ru-Ru coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) measurements... Fourier-transform EXAFS analysis... the peak at 1.5 Å can be attributed to Ru–O bonds, while the peak at 2.2 Å can be assigned to Ru–Ru bonds in Ru nanoclusters.
